{{Quote|I don't know if I've ever seen a droid save someone like that before&hellip; rather unusual behavior.|Yalta Val|<ref name="Legacy 5">[[Legacy (2013) 5|''Legacy'' (2013) 5]]</ref>}}
An '''Imperial communications droid''', sometimes called "'''comm droid'''" by his companions, played a significant role in the life of [[Ania Solo]] and her [[Darth Wredd's insurgency|hunt]] for the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Darth Wredd]] in the aftermath of the [[second Imperial Civil War]]. Originally assigned to the [[Imperial Knight]] [[Yalta Val]], the [[Imperial communications droid|comm droid]] was severely damaged when Val was [[Ambush in the Surd Nebula|ambushed]] in the [[Surd Nebula/Legends|Surd Nebula]], and he ended up as scrap in [[Ania Solo's junkyard|Solo's junkyard]]. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] retrieved [[Imperial Knight lightsaber|Val's lightsaber]] before fleeing from the [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]], however, and Solo's discovery of the [[Lightsaber/Legends|weapon]] set a tumultuous series of events into motion. The droid soon afterward became loyal to Imperial Knight [[Jao Assam]], and stuck by his ''de facto'' master's side while Assam and Solo tracked down Wredd.

==Biography==
===Going Solo===
{{Quote|RECONNOITER. CHECK FOR SURVIVORS. RETRIEVE. HOME.|The communications droid, retrieving Yalta Val's lightsaber from the planet Mala|<ref name="Legacy 1" />}}
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[138 ABY]], an [[Imperial communications droid]]<ref name="Legacy 1" /> with [[Gender/Legends|masculine]] [[Programmer/Legends|programming]]<ref name="Legacy 9" /> served the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]]. While on a mission to the [[Carreras system/Legends|Carreras system]] with the [[Imperial Knight]] [[Yalta Val]], the comm [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was sent out into the [[Surd Nebula/Legends|Surd Nebula]] to act as a beacon due the [[Nebula/Legends|nebula's]] blocking of communications. When [[Unidentified Nune-class shuttle variant|Val's shuttle]] crashed onto the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mala (planet)|Mala]], the Knight was [[Ambush in the Surd Nebula|ambushed]] by a [[Darth Wredd's master|Sith master]] and [[Darth Wredd|apprentice]] and taken [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]]. The comm droid checked for other survivors, found none, and then retrieved [[Imperial Knight lightsaber|Val's lightsaber]]. While rocketing away from the planet on a course for the Triumvirate's home base of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the droid was heavily damaged by tiny particles from the nebula. He made it only as far as the Carreras [[Star system/Legends|system]], where he ended up in the [[Ania Solo's junkyard|junkyard]] of one [[Ania Solo]].<ref name="Legacy 1" />

[[File:Findofthecentury.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ania Solo finds the communications droid in her junkyard.]]
One [[Standard week/Legends|week]] later, Solo discovered the droid and brought him to her friend [[Sauk]] on a [[Carreras Minor ice mining platform]], where the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] was uncovered from the droid's interior. Their attempts to sell the weapon led to a run-in with the law,<ref name="Legacy 1" /> and their successful escape in [[Ania Solo's starship|Solo's ship]] only ended up with them [[Carreras Incident|attacked]] by the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]]&mdash;[[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Wredd&mdash;at Solo's junkyard. The [[IG-series/Legends|IG-series]] droid [[AG-37]] ferried Solo and Saul offworld in [[AG-37's freighter|his freighter]], where Sauk, devastated at finding himself a [[Refugee/Legends|refugee]] and a criminal, tinkered with the comm droid and uncovered a [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of Yalta Val [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|dueling]] the [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]]. On AG-37's request, the comm droid enhanced the image of Val's lightsaber, and the group realized that it was the same weapon as the one they possessed.<ref name="Legacy 2" /> A flight from a sudden [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of [[Carreras starfighter]]s led the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] to Carreras Minor's surface, where Sauk was finally able to stabilize the comm droid's power source.<ref name="Legacy 3" />

When the Imperial Knight [[Jao Assam]], who was searching for his wayward comrade, showed up and saved the group from a [[Unidentified Carreras Minor tentacled serpent|tentacled serpent]], the now-functional comm droid flew out of the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] on his [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] and played the hologram for the newcomer. He then provided the coordinates for the planet Mala, but the group's rescue attempt was cut short when they were caught in the [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] of a [[Shifalan patrol ship]].<ref name="Legacy 3" /> The [[Shifala]]ns were following the orders of Darth Wredd, who was posing as Yalta Val, and Solo's group were all thrown into [[Prison/Legends|holding cells]] in the [[Carreras G51 communications array]]. The comm droid was the lone exception, as he managed to hide in a floor compartment aboard the freighter; when the coast was clear, he escaped into the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] where the freighter had been stored. Solo and her companions were freed by the Shifalan [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Biala]], who was tired of "Yalta Val" undermining her authority, but Wredd attacked the group in the hangar and severely injured most of them.<ref name="Legacy 4">[[Legacy (2013) 4|''Legacy'' (2013) 4]]</ref>

Jao Assam in particular was knocked out of the hangar and into the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]],<ref name="Legacy 4" /> but the comm droid followed, placing a [[Breath mask/Legends|breath mask]] onto the Imperial Knight's face and keeping him alive. Solo, having emerged from the battle relatively unscathed, hopped into [[Unidentified Galactic Triumvirate starfighter|Assam's starfighter]] and followed the departing Wredd to Mala, where she freed Yalta Val from his chains. Wredd was in the midst of using the [[Communications array/Legends|communications array]] to broadcast his declaration of an [[Darth Wredd's insurgency|insurgency]] against both the Triumvirate and the [[One Sith]], but Solo's intervention stopped him from killing Val in front of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], and the two [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]] [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|dueled]] briefly before the Sith fled. Solo, meanwhile, returned to the array and brought her injured comrades aboard AG-37's freighter; she then returned to Mala and picked up Val in [[Time/Legends|time]] to save him from the array, which Wredd had rigged to crash onto the planet's surface. As the freighter made its way out of the system, its crew came across Assam and the comm droid and brought them aboard.<ref name="Legacy 5" />

===On the hunt===
{{Quote|What's he doing?''"<br />"''Looks like he's reconfigured his antenna to keep broadcasting our signal at depth. Smart little guy.|Ania Solo and Jao Assam|<ref name="Legacy 9" />}}
Assam rested aboard the freighter, but the damaged vessel was unable to make [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]]. The comm droid repeatedly broadcasted a [[Distress signal/Legends|distress signal]], which was eventually picked up by the ''[[Animus]]'', a Triumvirate-aligned [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]. The [[Destroyer/Legends|Destroyer]] rescued the freighter and began to make its way to Coruscant, and the comm droid hovered through its corridors, eventually finding Assam recovering in a [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]]. At that moment, Assam experienced a [[Force vision/Legends|Force vision]] of Darth Wredd striking down his [[Empress/Legends|Empress]], [[Marasiah Fel]], and he resolved to [[Hunting/Legends|hunt]] for the wayward Sith despite explicit orders to the contrary from Her Imperial Majesty. Sauk and AG-37 departed from Solo's company aboard the latter's repaired freighter,<ref name="Legacy 6" /> but Solo, Assam, and the comm droid took a [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] and began their hunt, leaving with the reluctant blessing of Yalta Val. Their first stop was the planet [[Nalyd]], where a criminal database had revealed that [[Dieben]], a minion of Wredd's, had recently been extradited.<ref name="Legacy 7">[[Legacy (2013) 7|''Legacy'' (2013) 7]]</ref>

[[File:Broadcastfrombelow.jpg|thumb|right|350px|The comm droid broadcasts the depth of his group's sinking escape pod.]]
From Nalyd, the trail led to [[Dac/Legends|Dac]], a [[Water/Legends|water]] world whose [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] had been [[Final Protocol|poisoned]] during the recent [[Second Imperial Civil War|Imperial Civil War]]. In the [[Mon Calamari system/Legends|system]], the shuttle was attacked and taken apart by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], which caused its barely-functioning [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] to make a crash landing inside the [[Mon Calamari Orbital Shipyards]] that [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the dead world. After disposing of the pirates who boarded the shuttle, Solo and Assam began to explore the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]], with the comm droid in tow. When they found that the pirates were building a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] using [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] and [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] refugees as [[Slavery/Legends|slave labor]], the comm droid was ordered by Assam to send a message to Coruscant using Imperial encryption. The group was then discovered by the slaving ring's leader, the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Luft]]. The Sith threw Solo, Assam, the Mon Calamari [[Luen]], and the Quarren [[Tikin]] into an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]], and the comm droid quickly followed his friends inside before the pod was launched into the [[Viral spore|poisoned]] oceans of Dac.<ref name="Legacy 8">[[Legacy (2013) 8|''Legacy'' (2013) 8]]</ref>

As the pod sank, the comm droid reconfigured his antenna to continually broadcast the depth of the pod. The signal was picked up by AG-37 and Sauk, who were nearby, and the two were able to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] their freighter into Dac's oceans and recover the escape pod with a [[Power harpoon launcher|harpoon and tow cable]]. As the reunited group discussed their plans in a shipyard hangar, Tikin stormed back to his post rather than get involved. Assam resolved to take on Luft in order to locate Wredd, even as the others departed in the freighter to find reinforcements. The comm droid steadfastly followed Assam, but when Tikin betrayed their plot to Luft, Assam and the droid were discovered and forced to dodge a hail of [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] bolts. Tikin was killed by Luft despite his attempt to cooperate with the Sith, and as Assam confronted Luft, the furious Mon Calamari and Quarren slaves began to rise up against their captors. Meanwhile, a Triumvirate fleet led by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gar Stazi]] and Yalta Val&mdash;who had received the comm droid's message&mdash;arrived in-system and [[Battle of Dac (Darth Luft)|attacked]] the pirates.<ref name="Legacy 9" />

As Stazi flooded the shipyards with water from a [[Tanker/Legends|tanker]], the comm droid plotted an escape and made his way to a hatch, which he opened by [[Slicer/Legends|slicing]] into its controls. The water [[Crystal/Legends|crystallized]] into an ice plume as it escaped into space with him, but the droid avoided being frozen and stayed close to the shipyards' exterior as the battle raged. After receiving a request from Solo, he closed the doors to Bay 519C just in time to save her and a group of refugees from being sucked into space. The [[Death/Legends|death]] of Darth Luft at Assam's hands and the subduing of the pirates by Val's Imperial Knights and [[Aquatic assault stormtrooper|seatroopers]] ended the battle, and Solo's group re-embarked on their hunt for Darth Wredd. Their vehicle was the freighter of AG-37, who had decided that hunting for Wredd was the right thing to do. In the ship's cockpit, a message came through for Assam, and he, along with Solo, Sauk, AG-37, and the comm droid watched as a hologram of their target appeared.<ref name="Legacy 10" /> The renegade Sith had been systematically murdering members of the One Sith in an attempt to bring back the traditional Sith [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]],<ref name="Legacy 6" /> and he thanked Assam for taking out Luft and helping further his ultimate goals.<ref name="Legacy 10" />

===A sudden snatch===
{{Quote|AG thinks a micro-meteor got past the shield where it was weakened by that shockwave. It seems to have punctured the attenuating matrix around the fuel injection chamber. I'm sending this guy to see how bad the damage is.|Sauk, before sending the comm droid out into space|<ref name="Legacy 11" />}}
[[File:Narrowly_avoiding_ice_plume.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The comm droid narrowly avoiding an ice plume]]
During their hunt, the makeshift crew of AG-37's freighter found delivery work as part of their [[Captain/Legends|captain's]] shipping business. Early in the year [[139 ABY]], The comm droid was hovering outside of the ship's [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] as AG-37 piloted them through a precarious [[Mine/Legends|minefield]]. AG-37's success allowed them to land at [[Lasgo Port]] on their [[Unidentified planet (Lasgo Port)|target planet]] and deliver their goods, but to everyone's surprise, the group discovered a "Wanted" poster of Solo on the surface. Back in space, a micro-[[Meteor/Legends|meteor]] penetrated the freighter's [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]], which prompted Sauk to send the comm droid out into space to check on the damage. As the droid repaired the puncture, he noticed a commotion coming from a nearby derelict ship and proceeded to investigate&mdash;with the rest of his crew watching via his live [[Camera/Legends|camera]], the comm droid peered into the derelict's [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] panels and saw survivors. AG-37's crew immediately docked with the ship and provided it with [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. One of the survivors was [[Ramid]], and old friend of Solo's, but Ramid and his crew quickly kidnapped Solo and detached from AG-37's freighter. After detonating a mine<ref name="Legacy 11" /> that damaged AG-37's ship,<ref name="Legacy 12">[[Legacy (2013) 12|''Legacy'' (2013) 12]]</ref> Ramid escaped into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="Legacy 11" />

AG-37, Sauk, and Assam were able to repair the freighter<ref name="Legacy 12" /> and begin searching for Solo,<ref name="Legacy 13">[[Legacy (2013) 13|''Legacy'' (2013) 13]]</ref> and they were eventually able to locate Ramid's ship on a [[Unidentified planet (glass rain)|planet that sometimes rained glass]]. A search of the downed vessel revealed only corpses, none of them Solo's or Ramid's, and a sudden [[Glass/Legends|glass]] storm forced Sauk and Assam to seek refuge back in the freighter. AG-37, however, set out in the glass rain to locate their quarry. While his biological friends waited, the comm droid received a transmission from Yalta Val on Coruscant and played it for them. Val revealed that Solo was innocent of the crime for which she was being framed&mdash;the murder of Imperial Knight [[Teemen Alton]]&mdash;as Alton had been killed by someone with a [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetic hand]]. When AG-37 located Solo at the planet's only outpost, Sauk and Assam brought the freighter there, and Assam dismounted. Sauk was forced to take the ship above the clouds, however, as [[Acid rain/Legends|acid rain]] began to fall.<ref name="Legacy 14">[[Legacy (2013) 14|''Legacy'' (2013) 14]]</ref>.

The comm droid remained aboard AG-37's freighter while Jao Assam ventured into the settlement to rescue Ania Solo. There, Jao found that Ramid had been killed and that Ania was being attacked by an [[unidentified masked bounty hunter]], the real killer of the Imperial Knight whom Ania was alleged to have murdered.<ref name="Legacy 14" /> While Jao and Ania succeeded in killing the bounty hunter following a prolonged fight, Ania was subsequently arrested by a force of [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and brought back to Coruscant to face trial. However, Master Val and Jao Assam succeeded in clearing Ania's name by presenting evidence that Ania was not the real killer and that real killer, the bounty hunter, had a prosthetic hand. Following Ania's acquittal, the comm droid accompanied Sauk and AG-37 when they were reunited with Ania. However, Jao was arrested and imprisoned for the crime of deserting the Imperial Knights.<ref name="Legacy 15">[[Legacy (2013) 15|''Legacy'' (2013) 15]]</ref>

===Showdown with the Sith===
[[File:Ania_acquitted.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The comm droid was always seen with Ania and her companions]]
Following Ania Solo's kidnapping and rescue, the rogue Sith Darth Wredd resurfaced and kidnapped Jao Assam.<ref name="Legacy 15" /> The two of them then escaped Coruscant and headed for parts unknown. [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Empress]] Marasiah Fel then dispatched Ania, Sauk, AG-37, and a platoon of Trandoshan stormtroopers to rescue Jao Assam. The comm droid accompanied Ania and her companions on this mission to rescue Jao. Their quest took them to the floating world of Mala. Mala had been the former home world of Darth Wredd prior to its destruction towards the end of the Second Imperial Civil War. The One Sith had tested a [[Bioweapon/Legends|bioweapon]] on the planet, destroying all life on Mala and knocking the planet from its orbit. Darth Wredd was the sole survivor and was forced to join the One Sith but harbored a desire for vengeance against the Sith. After killing his master, Wredd had embarked on a one-man insurgency against the One Sith. He also intended to recruit Jao as his apprentice and to bring him over to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]].<ref name="Legacy 16">[[Legacy (2013) 16|''Legacy'' (2013) 16]]</ref>

Darth Wredd planned to lure the One Sith and Empress Fel to Mala where he intended to exact revenge against the Sith and to kill the Empress. Wredd tricked Jao into transmitting Mala's coordinates to Ania's rescue party, the One Sith, and Empress Fel. As planned, Ania and company discovered Mala and rescued Jao. During the rescue mission, the comm droid served as a torch light for the rescue party. The comm droid was also present during a [[Battle of the Floating World|fierce battle]] between Ania's rescue mission and a large One Sith army.<ref name="Legacy 17">[[Legacy (2013) 17|''Legacy'' (2013) 17]]</ref> Ania's mission was later reinforced by an army of Imperial Knights led by the Empress herself. The Imperial Knights succeeded in wiping out the One Sith army, thus playing into Darth Wredd's hands. Darth Wredd then attempted to assassinate Empress Fel but was thwarted and killed by Jao and Ania. The comm droid was present at the death of Darth Wredd and the reunion between Jao and Master Val. Following Jao's pardon, the Imperial Knight was allowed to resign from his Order and join Ania, Sauk, and AG-37. The comm droid accompanied Jao and Ania's company on their travels throughout the galaxy.<ref name="Legacy 18">[[Legacy (2013) 18|''Legacy'' (2013) 18]]</ref>

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|JAO DID COME TO THE CARRERAS SYSTEM BECAUSE THE DROID FAILED TO PATCH IN. PERHAPS IT FELT THAT JAO HAD TRAVELED ALL THAT WAY JUST TO RESCUE ''IT.'' SOMETIMES A DEBT OF GRATITUDE CAN WEIGH HEAVILY. EVEN ON A DROID.|AG-37|<ref name="Legacy 5" />}}
[[File:Dedication.jpg|thumb|left|275px|The droid rescues Jao Assam from deep space.]]
The Imperial communications droid, sometimes simply called "comm droid" by his companions,<ref name="Legacy 10" /> was small and spherical, not much bigger than the head of an average [[Human/Legends|Human]]. He hovered on repulsorlifts and was also equipped with sublight drives that enabled him to fly through the vacuum of space.<ref name="Legacy 1" /> As a communications droid, he could send and receive signals that could travel long distances,<ref name="Legacy 9" /> and he possessed both a [[Vidcam|video camera]]<ref name="Legacy 11" /> and a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]],<ref name="Legacy 2" /> each of which could both record and play.<ref name="Legacy 2" /><ref name="Legacy 11" /> The comm droid could also slice into electronic systems.<ref name="Legacy 10" /> Mostly light gray in color but with some green on his exterior, the droid also had a single blue [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptor]]. A large fin extended from the top of his frame, and four thin [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] protruded below,<ref name="Legacy 3" /> as did three electric lights.<ref name="Legacy 9" /> An additional limb could extend from the front of his frame that could be used to manipulate tools.<ref name="Legacy 5" /> Although he was described using masculine pronouns by some,<ref name="Legacy 9" /><ref name="Legacy 11" /> at least one other droid referred to him as "it."<ref name="Legacy 5" />

Although originally assigned to Yalta Val,<ref name="Legacy 1" /> and programmed to send messages that bore Val's personal stamp,<ref name="Legacy 9" /> the comm droid became quickly loyal to Jao Assam during the Carreras Incident. AG-37 posited that the droid believed Assam had come to Carreras just to rescue him, and that the droid consequently felt he owed a debt of gratitude to the Imperial Knight. The droid saved Assam from death by exposure to deep space,<ref name="Legacy 5" /> and he continued to follow Assam in the aftermath of Carreras, joining him on his hunt for Darth Wredd<ref name="Legacy 7" /> and staying aboard the Mon Calamari Shipyards with Assam after all of their friends had fled the yards to find reinforcements.<ref name="Legacy 9" /> The droid also voluntarily entered an escape pod with Assam that was bound for the [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] oceans of Dac,<ref name="Legacy 8" /> and from there broadcast a signal that ultimately led to the Imperial Knight's salvation. Assam thought his companion a "smart little guy."<ref name="Legacy 9" /> The comm droid displayed a dose of curiosity when he investigated a nearby derelict ship, despite his companions' insistence that there was no time to do so.<ref name="Legacy 11" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Despite her famous heritage, Ania Solo is just a girl trying to make her way in a galaxy gone bad. But it all gets worse when she comes into possession of a lightsaber and an Imperial communications droid—and discovers she has been targeted for death!|Solicitation for the first issue of ''Star Wars: Legacy Volume II''|<ref name="Solicitation">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/22-233/Star-Wars-Legacy-1|text=Star Wars: Legacy #1}}</ref>}}
The communications droid was created by authors [[Corinna Bechko]] and [[Gabriel Hardman]] as a character in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series ''[[Star Wars: Legacy Volume 2]]''. He was mentioned in the solicitation for the series' [[Legacy (2013) 1|first issue]],<ref name="Solicitation" /> and he has since appeared in every issue of the series save for its [[Legacy (2013) 12|twelfth]] and [[Legacy (2013) 13|thirteenth]]. He is, however, yet to receive a name. The droid has been drawn by both Hardman and [[Brian Albert Thies|Brian Thies]], and has been colored by [[Rachelle Rosenberg]] and [[Jordan Boyd]].

The comm droid appeared on a [[:File:Legacyphantom.jpg|phantom variant cover]] of ''Legacy''{{'s}} first issue that paid homage to [[:File:Star Wars Style A poster 1977.jpg|the classic 1977 poster]] for the [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|original ''Star Wars'' film]]. In the picture, the comm droid occupies space in the top left corner that in [[1977]] was taken by the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="Image comparison">Comparison of [[:File:Legacyphantom.jpg]] to [[:File:Star Wars Style A poster 1977.jpg]]</ref>
